I traced this through the source files. The page itself (`app/(chat)/chat/[id]/page.tsx`) returns `null`, so the wrapping comes entirely from the two layouts on its path.

- **`app/layout.tsx`** wraps the content in `ThemeProvider`, then `SessionProvider` (from next-auth, so not a project file), then `TooltipProvider`.
- **`app/(chat)/layout.tsx`** wraps it in `DataStreamProvider`, then React's `Suspense`, then a `SidebarShell` component defined in the same file. `SidebarShell` wraps the content in `SidebarProvider` and then `SidebarInset`.

I left out components that render beside the content rather than around it: `AppSidebar`, `Toaster`, `Script` and `ChatShell`/`ActiveChatProvider`. None of the wrapper components wraps the content in another project component.

{"answer": ["app/layout.tsx", "components/theme-provider.tsx", "components/ui/tooltip.tsx", "app/(chat)/layout.tsx", "components/chat/data-stream-provider.tsx", "components/ui/sidebar.tsx"]}

I found six routes that can render `PromptInputButton`. They are all public viewer pages under the Pages Router.

- **How it gets there:** The only file that imports from `components/ai-elements/prompt-input.tsx` is `ee/features/ai/components/viewer-chat-panel.tsx`, which renders `PromptInputButton` directly at line 722. That line falls after the start of `ViewerChatPanelContent` (line 203), and I assumed the exported `ViewerChatPanel` renders that inner component; I didn't open the file to confirm it.
- **Who renders the chat panel:** `ViewerChatPanel` is rendered by `ViewData` (`components/view/view-data.tsx:311`) and by `DataroomViewer` (`components/view/viewer/dataroom-viewer.tsx:1286`).
- **The next layer up:** `DocumentView` and `DataroomDocumentView` both render `ViewData`, and `DataroomView` renders `DataroomViewer`.
- **The pages:** `/view/[linkId]`, its `embed` page and the custom-domain versions under `/view/domains/[domain]/[slug]` render `DocumentView` or `DataroomView`. The two `/d/[documentId]` pages render `DataroomDocumentView`.

The branding pages only mention "document-view" and "dataroom-view" as tab names; they don't import these components, so they aren't included.

```json
{"answer": ["/view/[linkId]", "/view/[linkId]/embed", "/view/[linkId]/d/[documentId]", "/view/domains/[domain]/[slug]", "/view/domains/[domain]/[slug]/embed", "/view/domains/[domain]/[slug]/d/[documentId]"]}
```

Three files get edits: the declaring file and the two files that import `titleModel` from it.

- **`lib/ai/models.ts`**: the declaration on line 3.
- **`lib/ai/generate-title.ts`**: the import on line 4 and the use on line 21.
- **`lib/ai/providers.ts`**: the import on line 3 and the use on line 32.

These are left alone because they only share the name:
- **`lib/ai/models.mock.ts`** and **`lib/ai/models.test.ts`** each declare their own separate `titleModel`.
- **`lib/ai/providers.ts`, line 9**: here `titleModel: mockTitleModel` reads a property from `require("./models.mock")`, so it refers to the mock's export, not this one.

{"answer": ["lib/ai/models.ts", "lib/ai/generate-title.ts", "lib/ai/providers.ts"]}

I traced this by searching the source directly rather than using the code graph, and the result is two routes, both reached through one chain:

1. `SheetContent` is used in only one place: the mobile branch of `Sidebar` in `components/ui/sidebar.tsx:177`. Nothing else imports `components/ui/sheet`.
2. `<Sidebar>` is rendered only by `AppSidebar` in `components/chat/app-sidebar.tsx:86`.
3. `AppSidebar` is rendered only by `app/(chat)/layout.tsx:34`.
4. That layout wraps the two pages in the `(chat)` group: `app/(chat)/page.tsx` and `app/(chat)/chat/[id]/page.tsx`.

{"answer": ["/", "/chat/[id]"]}

I found five files: the file that declares `Artifact` (`components/chat/create-artifact.tsx:71`, `export class Artifact`) and the four artifact client files that import it by name. I listed them from text searches, not from an actual IDE rename. I found no re-exports. The other imports from `create-artifact` use only `ArtifactActionContext` and `ArtifactToolbarItem`, so a rename wouldn't touch those files.

{"answer": ["components/chat/create-artifact.tsx", "artifacts/code/client.tsx", "artifacts/image/client.tsx", "artifacts/sheet/client.tsx", "artifacts/text/client.tsx"]}

I searched the repo for the name and for every import of `lib/constants`. Only two files import `suggestions` from it, so a rename would change three files:

- `lib/constants.ts`: the declaration (line 15).
- `components/chat/preview.tsx`: the import (line 5) and the `suggestions.map(...)` use (line 65).
- `components/chat/suggested-actions.tsx`: the import (line 6) and its use at line 18.

The other matches for `suggestions` are local variables, props, string literals or separate modules like `lib/editor/suggestions`, so the rename leaves them alone.

{"answer": ["lib/constants.ts", "components/chat/preview.tsx", "components/chat/suggested-actions.tsx"]}

No other files import from the `yearly-recap` index, so the rename only needs to update the declaration, the re-export and the one direct import.

{"answer": ["components/yearly-recap/yearly-recap-modal.tsx", "components/yearly-recap/index.ts", "components/yearly-recap/yearly-recap-banner.tsx"]}

I searched the source for `YearlyRecapModal`. Three files would be edited: the declaring file, the barrel file that re-exports it without an alias, and the banner component that imports and renders it. Nothing imports the symbol through the barrel, so no other files are touched.

{"answer": ["components/yearly-recap/yearly-recap-modal.tsx", "components/yearly-recap/index.ts", "components/yearly-recap/yearly-recap-banner.tsx"]}

I traced these from the source files. `/unsubscribe` is not in `EXCLUDED_PATHS`, so `_app.tsx` uses the branch that wraps the page in `TeamProvider` and `UploadProgressProvider`. The page's outermost element is a plain `div`, so it adds no file. `TooltipProvider` re-exports a third-party primitive, but the export is declared in `components/ui/tooltip.tsx`, so I included that file.

{"answer": ["pages/_app.tsx", "components/providers/posthog-provider.tsx", "components/theme-provider.tsx", "components/ui/tooltip.tsx", "context/team-context.tsx", "context/upload-progress-context.tsx"]}

I searched the source for references to `/api/document`, skipping the graph folder and the handler file. Three files send requests to this exact route, including the `?id=` and `&timestamp=` variants:

- `components/chat/artifact.tsx` uses it as an SWR key at line 98 and in two calls at lines 157 and 176.
- `components/chat/document-preview.tsx` uses it as an SWR key at line 54.
- `components/chat/version-footer.tsx` uses it at lines 59 and 61; line 61 adds the `&timestamp=` query.

A second search for other ways of building the path found no more callers. I didn't open the surrounding code, so these lines aren't each labelled as a fetch call or a mutate call.

{"answer": ["components/chat/artifact.tsx", "components/chat/document-preview.tsx", "components/chat/version-footer.tsx"]}

I found six routes, all public viewer pages, that can render `ConversationDocumentContext`:

1. `ConversationDocumentContext` is rendered by `ConversationViewSidebar` (`ee/features/conversations/components/viewer/conversation-view-sidebar.tsx:314`).
2. That is wrapped by `ConversationSidebar` (`components/view/conversations/sidebar.tsx`).
3. `ConversationSidebar` is rendered by two navigation bars:
   - `Nav` (`components/view/nav.tsx:569`), used by most of the document viewers (PDF, image, video, Excel, Notion and so on). They are reached through `ViewData`, which `DocumentView` and `DataroomDocumentView` render.
   - `DataroomNav` (`components/view/dataroom/nav-dataroom.tsx:698`), reached through `DataroomViewer` and `DataroomView`.
4. Those views are rendered by the six page files listed below.

`ConversationDetailPage` in `ee/features/conversations/pages/conversation-detail.tsx` also renders the component, but no route imports it. The dataroom conversations route, `pages/datarooms/[id]/conversations/[conversationId]/index.tsx`, renders `ConversationOverview` instead, and that doesn't reach the component. No `app/` routes reach it either.

{"answer": ["/view/[linkId]", "/view/[linkId]/embed", "/view/[linkId]/d/[documentId]", "/view/domains/[domain]/[slug]", "/view/domains/[domain]/[slug]/embed", "/view/domains/[domain]/[slug]/d/[documentId]"]}

I traced every `LoaderIcon` use back to a route. Four routes can render it:

- **`/` and `/chat/[id]`**: both sit under `app/(chat)/layout.tsx`. That layout renders `AppSidebar`, which renders `SidebarHistory` and `SidebarUserNav`. Both show `LoaderIcon`: `SidebarHistory` in its "Loading..." footer, which appears until all chat history has loaded (`components/chat/sidebar-history.tsx:337`). `SidebarUserNav` uses it at `components/chat/sidebar-user-nav.tsx:76`.
- **`/login` and `/register`**: both pages render `SubmitButton`, which uses `LoaderIcon` at `components/chat/submit-button.tsx:29`.

There is no `pages/` directory, so no Pages Router routes apply.

{"answer": ["/", "/chat/[id]", "/login", "/register"]}
